{{recipe}}

In the southeastern United States, '''collard greens''' are frequently served as a side item. They are traditionally cooked in a pot of premade broth or water flavored with pork.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Ham|ham hocks]]
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* Sea [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] to taste
* 2 [[Cookbook:Quart|quarts]] water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] [[Cookbook:Collard Greens|collard greens]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]

== Procedure ==

# Place ham hocks, garlic cloves and a healthy [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of sea salt in the 2 quarts of water, and slowly bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in a large stew pot until the ham hocks become tender.
# Meanwhile, wash the greens thoroughly with cold water to remove dirt, and then wash them once in the vinegar (do not pat dry after vinegar wash). Next, remove the stems and shred the leaves into thin strips.
# When the water is boiling, add the greens by the handful and turn the temperature down to medium. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] the greens uncovered until they are quite tender and the broth has reduced.
# Serve with hot pepper vinegar, [[Cookbook:Tabasco Sauce|Tabasco]], or [[Cookbook:Red pepper flakes|red pepper flakes]].
